about: How Telugu is typed in Latin letters (these fitted weights describe chat; half of the transliterator's synthetic pairs are spelled from them, the other half from the fitted weights): native word -> canonical romanisation (the first spelling of every slot), weighted chat spellings, and the skeleton folds the romanised lookup keys on. Read by training/mlkb/langs/romanisation.py; the weights are fitted to Aksharantar tel (training/mlkb/langs/calibrate.py), whose only pairs outside the held-out test split are mined ones. Each table maps a letter (or a conjunct) to [spelling, weight] options, canonical first.

skeleton.about: Applied to typed Latin and to the canonical romanisation alike: lowercase a-z only; a final letter of `dropTrailing` after a vowel is dropped; the longest `replace` key at each position (else `letters`, else the letter itself); a symbol equal to the one before it is dropped (doubled letters); then a final vowel in `dropFinal` after a consonant is dropped.

looseSpelling.about: Which typed spellings spell a word out, for ranking (the engine's Romanisation::relaxed): `singles` read a letter as another, `pairs` read two letters in a row as one, `collapse` letters count once however often they repeat. Vowel length only: Telugu keeps d and t, g and k apart (ద త, గ క).

notes.inherent: The inherent vowel is a and is always said, so it is always typed (అమ్మ amma, తరగతి taragati): there is no schwa deletion, and a word ends in a virama only in loanwords (బస్ bas).
notes.anusvara: ం is the nasal of the stop after it inside a word (అందం andam, ఇంకా inka, పంపు pampu) and m at the end of a word (పుస్తకం pustakam). The tables have one spelling list for it wherever it stands, so the skeleton makes both readings one key: m before a consonant folds to n (the m + consonant entries of `replace`), and a final n or m after a vowel is dropped (dropTrailing). The price: a word that ends in n or m shares its key with the word without it.
notes.dentals: త is typed t or th (తెలుగు telugu / thelugu, తరువాత taruvata / tharuvatha) and ద d or dh; ట and డ are t and d. The skeleton folds th to t and dh to d, so త థ ట ఠ are one key letter, and ద ధ డ ఢ another.
notes.vowels: Long vowels are typed doubled about half the time (aa, ee, oo); ే and ో are mostly plain e and o. The skeleton folds aa, ee, ii, oo, uu, and ae and ea to e.
notes.letters: చ is ch, ఛ ch or chh, శ sh or s, ష sh, ఫ ph or f, వ v or w, ళ and ల l, ణ and న n, ఱ and ర r. ఋ and ృ are ru (కృష్ణ krushna) or ri (krishna). క్ష is ksh, జ్ఞ gn, jn or gy, శ్ర shr or sr.
notes.doubled: Doubled consonants are common and usually typed doubled (అక్క akka, చెప్పు cheppu); చ్చ is cch, chch or ch (వచ్చాడు vacchadu), త్త tt or tth, ద్ద dd or ddh.
notes.joiners: A ZWNJ after a virama (ఆన్‌లైన్) has no spelling: the walk skips it.
